- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a spike (e.g., 46.23 → 47.97), model fails to correct downward quickly; apply a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion adjustment.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits overconfidence; reduce forecast volatility by 15–20%.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values; apply a 3–5% downward adjustment for the first 7–10 days.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a peak (e.g., 48.60 → 44.29), model fails to anticipate; add a 2–3 day “cool-down” buffer in forecast decline.
- Model underestimates late-period drops (e.g., 47.22 → 40.35); apply a 10–15% downward correction for final 5–7 days if sentiment remains flat.
